newsitem.title: UK: British Gas denies manipulating gas prices.
newsitem.headline: British Gas denies manipulating gas prices.

text.p: British Gas Plc on Monday denied market rumours that it had deliberately cut production at its Morecambe Bay field to push spot natural gas prices higher.
"We're not fixing the price," said a spokesman at British Gas Trading.
The north and south Morecambe Bay gas fields, which supply about 15 percent of total UK gas demand, have been closed for maintenance and because of slow demand for most of the summer.
Production resumed on Thursday after a three-month shutdown as demand picked up slightly, British Gas said.
Industry regulator Ofgas said it was looking into the price fixing rumours as part of its ongoing monitoring of gas markets following recent changes in trading practices.
"Obviously we are concerned," an Ofgas spokesman said in reaction to the price fixing talk.
He added that any price manipulation by British Gas might contravene anti-competition regulations.
The British Gas spokesman, meanwhile, said thin trading conditions made it impossible to manipulate prices to the utility's own advantage.
"Yes, prices are higher now, but they would collapse as soon as we would try to sell any large volumes," the spokesman said.
Prices in the spot market peaked in mid-September at just over 17 pence per therm for delivery early next year compared with a price of around 14 pence early in June for the same period.
